title: North vs. South | The Great English Divide
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上奇妙而不可思议的事物，一边提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the north/south divide.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊英格兰的南北差异。

sentences.en: One way of dividing England is by whether you are a northerner or a southerner, whether you come from the north or the south of the country.
sentences.zh: 划分英格兰的一种方式，就是看你是北方人还是南方人，也就是看你来自这个国家的北部还是南部。

sentences.en: But as you will see, it is not simple, not simple at all, and this story will touch on British history, economics, politics, society, culture and more.
sentences.zh: 但正如你将看到的，这绝非一件简单的事，这个故事将涉及英国的历史、经济、政治、社会、文化等诸多方面。

sentences.en: It is also, I should add, part of a three-part mini-series we’re making on British divisions.
sentences.zh: 我还想补充一点，这也是我们关于英国内部隔阂的三集迷你系列节目之一。

sentences.en: In part one, we talked about the thousand-year rivalry between Scotland and England, and in part three we talked about The Wars Of The Roses.
sentences.zh: 在第一集里，我们谈到了苏格兰和英格兰之间长达千年的宿怨，而在第三集里，我们讨论了玫瑰战争（The Wars Of The Roses）。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get started and talk about The Great British Divide.
sentences.zh: 好，那我们就切入正题，来聊聊“英国的大分歧”。

sentences.en: In 2008, a professor at the University of Sheffield published a startling discovery.
sentences.zh: 2008年，谢菲尔德大学的一位教授发表了一项令人吃惊的发现。

sentences.en: Professor Danny Dorling had drawn, he had mapped out from west to east, a line that divided England.
sentences.zh: Danny Dorling 教授自西向东画出了一条将英格兰一分为二的线。

sentences.en: To the north of the line was “the North”.
sentences.zh: 这条线以北是“北方”。

sentences.en: To the south of the line, “the South”. Now, this wasn’t a revolutionary division, it wasn’t a division that Professor Dorling created himself.
sentences.zh: 这条线以南则是“南方”。当然，这并不是什么颠覆性的划分，也不是 Dorling 教授凭空捏造出来的。

sentences.en: For centuries people in England had referred to themselves as either Southerners or Northerners, but nobody could quite agree on where the line that divided one from the other was.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，英格兰人一直自称南方人或北方人，但对于划分两者的分界线究竟在哪里，大家始终未能达成一致。

sentences.en: It probably started somewhere close to southern Wales, and then went east and north.
sentences.zh: 它大概始于威尔士南部附近的某个地方，然后向东、向北延伸。

sentences.en: It was a fuzzy, unclear line, in people’s minds at least.
sentences.zh: 至少在人们的心中，这是一条模糊不清的界线。

sentences.en: But some cities were unanimously agreed to be southern or northern.
sentences.zh: 但有些城市被公认属于南方或北方。

sentences.en: London was southern. Manchester, Leeds and Newcastle were northern.
sentences.zh: 伦敦属于南方。曼彻斯特、利兹和纽卡斯尔属于北方。

sentences.en: But there was no defining line, there was no geographical line, like a river or a range of mountains, no political line where one part started and another ended, nothing that clearly marked where the north ended and the south started.
sentences.zh: 但这里并没有一条明确的分界线，没有像河流或山脉那样的地理分界线，也没有标志着一部分结束、另一部分开始的政治分界线，没有任何东西能明确标出北方在哪里结束、南方在哪里开始。

sentences.en: Wherever this line was, it was also not a straight line but one that went northeast at an almost 45-degree angle, so, strangely enough, some “northern” cities were further south than “southern” cities.
sentences.zh: 无论这条线在哪里，它都不是一条直线，而是以接近45度的角度向东北延伸，因此奇怪的是，有些“北方”城市实际上比“南方”城市还要靠南。

sentences.en: Plus, there was the complication that there is a region of the country called “The Midlands”, which insisted it was its own region but was often called south by Northerners and north by Southerners.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个复杂之处：英国有一个被称为“中部地区”（The Midlands）的区域，该地区坚持认为自己是一个独立的区域，但北方人常称其为南方，南方人又常称其为北方。

sentences.en: Anyway, the point is that any line, any division, was fuzzy, unclear.
sentences.zh: 总之，关键在于任何界线、任何划分都是模糊不清的。

sentences.en: Where there was unanimous agreement, however, was that there was a division.
sentences.zh: 然而，大家一致认同的是，这种分歧确实存在。

sentences.en: The north was not the same as the south.
sentences.zh: 北方和南方截然不同。

sentences.en: Life was different, the people were different, people spoke with different accents, they used different words, they did different jobs, they drank different types of beer, they wore different clothes, they had different lives.
sentences.zh: 生活不同，人也不同，人们说话口音各异，用词不同，从事的工作不同，喝的啤酒种类不同，穿的衣服不同，过着截然不同的生活。

sentences.en: Northerners and Southerners were both English, but they were very different people.
sentences.zh: 北方人和南方人虽然都是英格兰人，但他们是非常不同的人群。

sentences.en: So, in this episode, we will explore the question of both what, where and why.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这一集里，我们将探讨“是什么”、“在哪里”以及“为什么”。

sentences.en: What are some common differences between people from the south and the north, how many of these are just stereotypes, and how many are really true?
sentences.zh: 南方人和北方人有哪些常见的差异，其中有多少只是刻板印象，又有多少是真实存在的？

sentences.en: Where does this division lie, and how can you tell whether you are in the north or the south of the country?
sentences.zh: 这条分界线在哪里，你又该如何判断自己身处该国的北方还是南方呢？

sentences.en: And why do these divisions exist? Let’s start with some common differences between northerners and southerners, and for this we are actually going to turn to the words of George Orwell, in his book The Road to Wigan Pier.
sentences.zh: 为什么会存在这些分歧呢？让我们先从北方人和南方人的一些常见差异说起，为此我们不妨借用 George Orwell 在其著作《通往维冈码头之路》（The Road to Wigan Pier）中的话。

sentences.en: In other words, the Northern man considers himself to be a real man doing real industrial work.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，北方男人认为自己是从事真正的工业劳动的真汉子。

sentences.en: And he considers Southern men to be snobs, doing easy work.
sentences.zh: 而他认为南方男人是势利眼，干着轻松的差事。

sentences.en: And the Southern man looks down on his Northern counterpart as something of a savage, an uncivilised barbarian.
sentences.zh: 南方男人则瞧不起北方人，把他们看作未开化的野蛮人。

sentences.en: They are both British, both English even, but they feel little sense of kinship, given their differences.
sentences.zh: 他们都是英国人，甚至都是英格兰人，但鉴于这些差异，他们之间几乎没有什么亲近感。

sentences.en: This was written in 1937, and this broad theme has continued to this very day.
sentences.zh: 写下这段话是在1937年，而这一大致的基调一直延续到了今天。

sentences.en: There was a really good BBC documentary from 1970 with an interview of a southern woman who married a northern man.
sentences.zh: 1970年有一部非常出色的 BBC 纪录片，采访了一位嫁给北方男人的南方女性。

sentences.en: She talks about her experience living in the north, and how none of the women cooked their children any proper food; they would either give them money for fish and chips or cook them something all in one pan, and then the poor children would have to eat out of the pan, they would have no plates.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了自己在北方的生活经历，说那里的女人们从不给孩子做一顿像样的饭菜；她们要么给孩子钱去买炸鱼薯条，要么把所有东西放在一个锅里乱炖，然后可怜的孩子们只能直接从锅里抓着吃，连盘子都没有。

sentences.en: And then the BBC journalist went to the north to ask the northerners about their view of the south, and they responded that Southerners are snobs, they go out to eat at restaurants because they can’t cook for themselves, and that they wouldn’t even dream of living in the south because it sounds so awful.
sentences.zh: 接着，BBC 记者去北方询问北方人对南方的看法，他们回答说南方人都是势利眼，他们去餐馆吃饭是因为自己不会做饭，而且北方人做梦都没想到过去南方生活，因为南方听起来太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And even to this very day, you can find videos on YouTube where people go to the streets of London or Manchester, Leeds or Newcastle and ask people what they think of their Southern or Northern counterparts and you will hear very similar things.
sentences.zh: 甚至直到今天，你依然可以在 YouTube 上看到这样的视频：人们走上伦敦、曼彻斯特、利兹或纽卡斯尔的街头，询问人们对南方或北方同胞的看法，你会听到非常相似的回答。

sentences.en: So, where does this come from? Well, to understand this we need to have a brief history lesson.
sentences.zh: 那么，这种差异从何而来？要想了解这一点，我们需要简单回顾一下历史。

sentences.en: For the purposes of this episode, we need to go back to the Industrial Revolution, which started in Britain in the mid-18th century.
sentences.zh: 就本集节目而言，我们需要回到18世纪中叶在英国爆发的工业革命。

sentences.en: Long story short, people from the countryside flocked to the cities to work in factories, producing everything from textiles to tools to iron.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，乡村人口涌入城市进入工厂工作，生产从纺织品、工具到钢铁的一切物品。

sentences.en: Britain transitioned from an agrarian, farming-based economy, to an industrial one.
sentences.zh: 英国从以农业为基础的经济体转变为工业经济体。

sentences.en: Although the capital and dominant city was London, the Industrial Revolution led to huge growth of cities outside the capital.
sentences.zh: 尽管首都和主导城市是伦敦，但工业革命推动了首都以外城市的巨大发展。

sentences.en: And particularly so in the north of the country, which had better access to natural resources, better rivers to power the mills and later transport goods, and better access to ports.
sentences.zh: 在英国北部尤其如此，那里更容易获取自然资源，拥有更好的河流来为工厂提供动力并在日后运输货物，而且更便于通往港口。

sentences.en: Birmingham, for example, went from a population of 15,000 in 1700 to 75,000 a hundred years later, and over half a million a hundred years after that.
sentences.zh: 例如伯明翰，其人口在1700年为1.5万人，一百年后增至7.5万人，再过一百年后更是超过了50万。

sentences.en: Manchester, Liverpool, and Newcastle, these were all cities at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, cities which grew both in size and wealth during the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentences.zh: 曼彻斯特、利物浦和纽卡斯尔，这些都是处于工业革命核心的城市，在18和19世纪期间，它们的规模和财富都大幅增长。

sentences.en: The north was industrial, factories, mines, dominated by manual labour.
sentences.zh: 北方是工业化的，布满了工厂、矿井，以体力劳动为主。

sentences.en: Life was tough, long hours doing often dangerous work in a factory or down a coal mine, but at least it was predictable, once you had a job, it would be a job for life.
sentences.zh: 生活很艰苦，人们要在工厂或煤矿井下从事长时间、往往还很危险的工作，但至少生活是可预测的，一旦有了工作，那就是一辈子的铁饭碗。

sentences.en: But moving into the 20th century, especially after World War I, the industries that had powered the North were in decline.
sentences.zh: 但进入20世纪，特别是一战之后，曾经推动北方发展的那些产业开始走下坡路。

sentences.en: Coal mining, steel production, shipbuilding.
sentences.zh: 煤炭开采、钢铁制造、造船业。

sentences.en: These were industries that Britain had excelled in in the 19th century and had been able to sell its products around the world.
sentences.zh: 这些都是英国在19世纪傲视全球并能将产品畅销世界各地的支柱产业。

sentences.en: But in the 20th century, British products were no longer so competitive.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪，英国产品不再那么具有竞争力。

sentences.en: Countries invested in their own steel and coal industries, and there was a diminishing need for British products.
sentences.zh: 各国纷纷投资本国的钢铁和煤炭产业，对英国产品的需求也日渐减少。

sentences.en: Initially, these British industries were supported financially by the government.
sentences.zh: 起初，这些英国产业得到了政府的财政支持。

sentences.en: If they went out of business, millions of jobs would be at risk, so the government continued to prop up these struggling industries.
sentences.zh: 如果它们倒闭，数百万个工作岗位将岌岌可危，因此政府继续扶持这些苦苦挣扎的产业。

sentences.en: The south of England, on the other hand, which had never been so dominated by industry, transitioned into a more service-based economy: finance, law, technology, professional services, all sectors of the economy that were more profitable, and more competitive in a globalising world.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，从未被重工业深度主导的英格兰南部，转型为了更偏向服务型的经济体：金融、法律、科技、专业服务，这些都是在日益全球化的世界中更具盈利能力和竞争力的经济部门。

sentences.en: Then, in the late 1970s, Britain got a new Prime Minister: Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 随后在20世纪70年代末，英国迎来了一位新首相：Margaret Thatcher。

sentences.en: She was a Conservative, both by political allegiance and in her fiscal beliefs.
sentences.zh: 无论在政治归属还是财政理念上，她都是一名保守派。

sentences.en: In other words, she represented the Conservative party and she believed in small government, that individuals and businesses should be responsible for themselves; the government should not support them by subsidising their life or business.
sentences.zh: 换言之，她代表保守党，信奉“小政府”理念，认为个人和企业应当自负盈亏；政府不应该通过补贴来保障他们的生活或扶持其企业。

sentences.en: And you may know what happened next. Margaret Thatcher started the process of closing the coal mines, which were mostly found in the north of the country.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道接下来发生了什么。Margaret Thatcher 开启了关闭煤矿的进程，而这些煤矿大部分分布在该国北部。

sentences.en: There was a large battle between Thatcher and the coal miners, and eventually, after almost a year of strikes, Thatcher won, and then embarked on a series of privatisation measures, shutting down unprofitable mines and factories and selling off everything from railroads to utility companies to private investors.
sentences.zh: Thatcher 与煤矿工人展开了一场激烈的较量，最终在经历近一年的罢工后，Thatcher 获胜，随后推行了一系列私有化措施，关闭了亏损的矿山和工厂，并将从铁路到公用事业公司的所有资产出售给私人投资者。

sentences.en: The result was a huge loss of jobs in these industries, which were concentrated in the north.
sentences.zh: 其结果是这些集中在北方的产业损失了大量工作岗位。

sentences.en: Unemployment shot up, reaching 13% across the UK, as 2 million people in the UK were out of work.
sentences.zh: 失业率飙升，全英失业率达到13%，有200万英国人失去了工作。

sentences.en: And this was particularly concentrated in towns and cities which had been dominated by coal mines, which were predominantly found in the north of England and in southern Wales.
sentences.zh: 而这种情况尤其集中在那些由煤矿主导的城镇和城市，这些地方主要分布在英格兰北部和威尔士南部。

sentences.en: And in many cases, these areas have never recovered economically.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，这些地区的经济至今未能恢复。

sentences.en: There are stark wage and productivity gaps between the North and the South, with people in London earning an average of ⅓ more than their Northern counterparts, and productivity of workers in London being 40% higher than those in the North.
sentences.zh: 南北之间存在巨大的工资和生产率差距，伦敦人的平均收入比北方同胞高出三分之一，而伦敦工人的生产率比北方工人高出40%。

sentences.en: We talked a bit in the previous episode about the resentment felt by some Scots towards the English for the perceived control that Westminster has over Scotland, but it is exactly the same in the north of England.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集聊到了部分苏格兰人对英格兰人的不满，因为他们觉得威斯敏斯特控制了苏格兰，但在英格兰北部，情况如出一辙。

sentences.en: The seat of political power is London, and people in the North often complain that politicians in Westminster do not care about them and that there is inadequate investment in the north of England.
sentences.zh: 政治权力的中心在伦敦，北方人经常抱怨威斯敏斯特的政客不关心他们，而且对英格兰北部的投资严重不足。

sentences.en: They have a point. The north of England is poorly connected from a public transport perspective, especially in smaller towns and cities.
sentences.zh: 他们抱怨得不无道理。从公共交通的角度来看，英格兰北部的交通连接很差，尤其是在小城镇和中小型城市。

sentences.en: Education spending tends to be lower in the North than in the South.
sentences.zh: 北方的教育支出往往也低于南方。

sentences.en: And, as you might expect, this has a real knock-on effect.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所料，这产生了实实在在的连锁反应。

sentences.en: Salaries are lower, there are fewer job opportunities, fewer opportunities for investment or grants for starting new businesses.
sentences.zh: 薪资更低，工作机会更少，获得创业投资或补助金的机会也更少。

sentences.en: And there is a large gap between north and south not just in economic and educational opportunities, but in life expectancy.
sentences.zh: 南北之间的巨大差距不仅体现在经济和教育机会上，还体现在人均预期寿命上。

sentences.en: In the southeast of the country, the most prosperous region of England, the life expectancy at birth is 80.1, whereas in the northeast, where it is lowest, it is 77.2.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰最繁华的东南部地区，出生时的预期寿命为80.1岁，而在寿命最短的东北部地区，仅为77.2岁。

sentences.en: And if we drill down even further the differences are even greater.
sentences.zh: 如果进一步细分对比，差异还会更大。

sentences.en: In Blackpool, which is incidentally where my father was born, the life expectancy at birth is 73, but in Cambridgeshire, in the southeast, it is 83.
sentences.zh: 在黑池（顺便提一句，那是我父亲出生的地方），出生时的预期寿命是73岁，而在东南部的剑桥郡，这一数字是83岁。

sentences.en: It is quite horrific to put it like that, but the average child in Blackpool will live 10 fewer years than one born in Cambridgeshire.
sentences.zh: 这样说可能有些触目惊心，但黑池的孩子平均要比剑桥郡出生的孩子少活10年。

sentences.en: Now, you might be listening to this thinking “Well, my country has divisions too”.
sentences.zh: 听到这里，你可能会想：“其实我所在的国家也有地域差异。”

sentences.en: The north vs south of Italy, or East vs.
sentences.zh: 比如意大利的北方与南方，或者东德与……

sentences.en: West Germany, for example. But neither of those are as extreme as in the UK.
sentences.zh: ……西德。但这两种情况都不像英国这样极端。

sentences.en: According to one report from 2019, ‘the UK is more regionally divided than any comparable advanced economy’.
sentences.zh: 根据2019年的一份报告，“在所有同类发达经济体中，英国的区域分化是最严重的”。

sentences.en: In this report, the researchers found that rates of mortality vary more within the UK than in the majority of developed nations, and that there are some places in the UK, like Blackpool and Manchester, which have mortality rates that are worse than those in parts of Turkey, Slovakia and Romania.
sentences.zh: 在这份报告中，研究人员发现，英国国内的死亡率差异超过了大多数发达国家，英国的一些地方（如黑池和曼彻斯特）的死亡率甚至比土耳其、斯洛伐克和罗马尼亚的部分地区还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Now, no offence to any wonderful people living in Turkey, Slovakia or Romania, but the GDP per capita of the UK is more than double that of Slovakia, triple that of Romania and four times that of Turkey, so given the wealth that exists in the country, the health outcomes for citizens should be better.
sentences.zh: 无意冒犯生活在土耳其、斯洛伐克或罗马尼亚的优秀人民，但英国的人均 GDP 是斯洛伐克的两倍多、罗马尼亚的三倍、土耳其的四倍，因此鉴于该国的财富水平，国民的健康状况本应更好才是。

sentences.en: There have been various government initiatives to try to fix this disparity, and reduce the economic gap between north and south.
sentences.zh: 政府曾出台多项举措试图纠正这种不均衡，缩小南北之间的经济差距。

sentences.en: Most recently, the former Prime Minister Boris Johnson campaigned on a message of “levelling up”, and increasing government spending in the north of the country, but according to most northern commentators, very little real progress has been made.
sentences.zh: 最近，前首相 Boris Johnson 以“均富升级”（levelling up）和增加对北部地区的政府支出为口号进行竞选，但在大多数北方评论员看来，实际取得的实质进展微乎其微。

sentences.en: Now, we must move on to talk about language and culture, because I think this will be more interesting for you than me reciting figures about mortality rates or productivity statistics.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们必须转入语言和文化方面的话题了，因为我觉得这比我在这儿念叨死亡率或生产率的统计数据要有趣得多。

sentences.en: I mentioned at the start of the episode that a university professor had produced a paper where he diligently mapped out the exact division between North and South, which was based on a complicated set of criteria.
sentences.zh: 我在节目开始时提到过，一位大学教授曾发表过一篇论文，基于一套复杂的标准，严谨地绘制出了南北之间的确切分界线。

sentences.en: A polling company called YouGov once tried to draw the line based on a simple question: it asked people what they call the meal that they have at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 民调公司 YouGov 曾尝试根据一个简单的问题来划线：他们问人们怎么称呼一天结束时吃的那顿饭。

sentences.en: If they called it “dinner”, they were from the south, and if they called it “tea”, they were from the north.
sentences.zh: 如果叫“dinner”，那就是南方人；如果叫“tea”，那就是北方人。

sentences.en: The polling company surveyed 42,000 people and split the country based on whether people were more likely to call it dinner or tea.
sentences.zh: 这家民调公司调查了4.2万人，并根据人们更倾向于叫 dinner 还是 tea 划分了整个国家。

sentences.en: And the result was pretty similar to the map that the university professor had presumably spent thousands of hours carefully crafting.
sentences.zh: 结果与那位大学教授大概花费数千小时精心制作的地图非常相似。

sentences.en: And this is just one vocabulary example.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是词汇方面的一个例子。

sentences.en: Accents are different, with southern accents typically having a long “a” in words like “bath” or “laugh”, and northern accents shortening them, like “bath” and “laff”.
sentences.zh: 口音也不同，南方口音通常在“bath”或“laugh”这类词中发长音“a”，而北方口音则发短音，读成“bath”和“laff”。

sentences.en: In several northern dialects speakers drop the direct article, or just shorten it to “t”, so instead of saying “in the bath”, they might say “in’t bath”.
sentences.zh: 在几种北方方言中，说话者会省略定冠词，或者将其缩略为“t”，所以他们不说“in the bath”，而是可能会说成“in’t bath”。

sentences.en: What’s more, in several northern dialects people will drop the “h” at the start of a word, saying “ave” instead of “have”, “art” instead of “heart”, and so on.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，在几种北方方言中，人们还会省略词首的“h”音，把“have”说成“ave”，把“heart”说成“art”，等等。

sentences.en: Now, these are just a few examples. There is a huge variety of different vocabulary used not just in the south vs the north, but a variety within both regions themselves.
sentences.zh: 这些只是其中的几个例子。不仅南北之间使用的词汇差异巨大，而且这两个地区内部本身的词汇也千差万别。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons that some Northerners feel animosity towards their Southern counterparts was because of a presumed institutional prejudice that speaking with a Northern accent and using Northern vocabulary was somehow inferior to speaking with a Southern accent.
sentences.zh: 某些北方人对南方同胞抱有敌意的原因之一，在于一种公认的体制性偏见：操北方口音、使用北方词汇在某种程度上被视为不如操南方口音高雅。

sentences.en: For a long time, until really the early 21st century, the BBC, the country’s national broadcaster, required all of its broadcasters to speak in a certain way, in a southern way, similar to the accent that I have, as I am from the south of the country.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，实际上直到21世纪初，国家广播机构 BBC 都要求其所有播音员以特定方式播音，即南方口音——就和我现在的口音差不多，因为我来自该国南部。

sentences.en: Northern journalists knew that they needed to adjust their accent, to soften it to sound less Northern, in order to get ahead in their careers.
sentences.zh: 北方记者心知肚明，他们必须调整自己的口音，将其弱化以显得不那么“北方”，这样才能在职业生涯中出人头地。

sentences.en: This thankfully has now changed, the BBC encourages a variety of accents, and it now has a headquarters in Manchester, but while I was growing up at least, everyone you heard on the BBC spoke in a particular way; they spoke like a Southerner.
sentences.zh: 值得庆幸的是，现在情况已经改变了，BBC 鼓励多元口音，并且现在在曼彻斯特也设有总部，但至少在我成长的年代，你在 BBC 上听到的每个人说话都是同一个调调；听起来都像南方人。

sentences.en: Now, every country, no matter how big or small, has its divisions, friendly rivalries between people from different regions.
sentences.zh: 无论国家大小，每个国家都有其内部差异以及不同地区人民之间的友好竞争。

sentences.en: England is no exception, although the line between north and south is not nearly as clear as some people might think it is.
sentences.zh: 英格兰也不例外，尽管南北之间的界线远没有某些人想象的那么分明。

sentences.en: There are no signs saying welcome to the north or welcome to the south, no river you cross or mountain range you need to go through.
sentences.zh: 那里没有写着“欢迎来到北方”或“欢迎来到南方”的指示牌，没有你需要跨越的河流，也没有必须翻越的山脉。

sentences.en: If you are travelling in England and you are unsure whether you’re in the north or south, let me suggest to you a foolproof way.
sentences.zh: 如果你在英格兰旅行，不确定自己是在北方还是南方，我来给你支一个万无一失的招数。

sentences.en: Take out a piece of paper and draw a picture of someone eating fish and chips in that white porcelain thing you wash yourself in, and ask a passerby what is going on.
sentences.zh: 拿出一张纸，画一个人在洗澡用的那个白色陶瓷浴缸里吃炸鱼薯条，然后问问路人这幅画在干什么。

sentences.en: If they say that someone is having their dinner in the bath, you’re probably in the south.
sentences.zh: 如果他们说有人在浴缸里吃晚餐（having their dinner in the bath），你大概是在南方。

sentences.en: If they say they’re “aving ‘t tea in’t bath”, you’re probably in the north.
sentences.zh: 如果他们说“aving ‘t tea in’t bath”，那你大概就是在北方了。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the north-south divide of England.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于英格兰南北差异的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，也希望你学到了新知识。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought about this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对本期节目的看法。

sentences.en: What areas of England have you been to? Were you aware of a north-south divide?
sentences.zh: 你去过英格兰的哪些地区？你之前了解这种南北差异吗？

sentences.en: What divisions are there in your country, if any?
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，你们国家存在什么样的地域差异呢？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so let’s get this discussion started.
sentences.zh: 我很想了解，所以让我们开启讨论吧。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的听众热烈交流。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 出品的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家一切安好，我们下期节目再见。

sentences.en: [END OF EPISODE]
sentences.zh: [本集结束]
